newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium mulls flight to Burundi - foreign ministry.
newsitem.headline: Belgium mulls flight to Burundi - foreign ministry.

text.p: Belgium confirmed on Friday it was considering organising a flight to the isolated central African state of Burundi to help its nationals leave.
"We have 305 nationals there, mainly civilians. We have written to them saying if they would like to leave they should let us know by September 20," a foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters.
The Belgian embassy in Bujumbura said on Thursday it was making arrangements in the light of deteriorating conditions in the country.
"There's no urgency. It's not an evacuation. It's just to offer them the chance to leave because at the moment they cannot," the foreign ministry spokesman said.
Burundi has been progressively cut off from the outside world since an army-led coup installed Pierre Buyoya as president in July. Belgian and other foreign nationals have been urged to leave.
The last commercial flight to Brussels from Burundi by Belgian airline Sabena SA was on August 13. Prior to the coup, Sabena flew to Burundi twice a week.
The United States organised a C130 military plane to allow some embassy officials to leave on September 4.
The Belgian foreign ministry spokesman said it had not been decided whether to charter a commercial aircraft or use a military plane in the event of a new flight.
"It depends on the response we get and the timing (of a flight)," he said.
